extracted.intended_audience: machine learning and formal-methods researchers (LLM + theorem proving community)
extracted.subtask_description: Evaluation and benchmarking of large language models (LLMs) for solving mathematical theorem-proving problems in an auto-active verifier (Dafny), including the translation of the miniF2F benchmark and empirical comparisons of automation vs. LLM guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation of miniF2F to Dafny
rubrics_metrics.description: MINIF2F-DAFNY: the first translation of the widely-used mathematical benchmark miniF2F to an auto-active verifier: Dafny.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a concrete benchmark target for measuring LLM performance in an auto-active verification setting; benchmark is available on GitHub (link in paper).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dafny automation success (empty proofs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Dafny's automation alone solves 39–44% of problems with empty proofs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measures the baseline capability of the auto-active verifier without additional proof guidance; used to quantify how many problems require human/LLM guidance versus being solvable by automation alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLM-assisted problem-solving success rate
rubrics_metrics.description: For the remaining problems, evaluation of 7 off-the-shelf LLMs achieved 55.7% success with the best model (Claude Sonnet 4.5) using modest resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the primary empirical metric for the paper: percentage of benchmark problems solved when LLMs provide high-level guidance to the verifier; reported as aggregate success and compared across models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparison across multiple LLMs
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation conducted over 7 off-the-shelf LLMs to compare effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cross-model comparison is used to identify best-performing models and to assess variability; the paper highlights the best model and reports aggregate success (55.7%).

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of labor: LLM guidance vs. automation
rubrics_metrics.description: Effective division of labor: LLMs provide high-level guidance while automation handles low-level details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Conceptual criterion guiding system design and evaluation — success is judged not only by solved problems but by how responsibilities split between LLM reasoning and verifier automation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practicality / resource usage
rubrics_metrics.description: LLM-guided approach succeeded using modest resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Resource efficiency (compute, time, or configuration simplicity) is reported and used as an implicit criterion for practicality of the approach.

rubrics_metrics.name: Need for substantial proof guidance in ITPs
rubrics_metrics.description: Many problems require substantial proof guidance in interactive theorem provers (ITPs), contrasted with Dafny's higher automation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a contextual evaluative point: the benchmark demonstrates differences in how much low-level guidance is needed across verification paradigms, informing interpretation of success rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Benchmark reproducibility and availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The benchmark and related artifacts are made available (GitHub link provided).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Availability is treated as a quality criterion for the work: providing code/data enables independent replication and further evaluation.
